concept.name: Context Compression for RAG

relationships.description: Connects Context Compression for RAG to llm prompt engineering in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: Techniques that prune, rerank, or summarize retrieved RAG chunks before LLM generation to slash token cost and TTFT while beating 'lost-in-the-middle' attention decay.
spark.keyTakeaway: Pair a fast cross-encoder reranker (BGE-Reranker-v2-M3) with token-level or extractive compression (LLMLingua-2 / RECOMP) to shrink 20k+ retrieved tokens down to 2k–3k high-signal tokens without losing exact citations.

concept.whyItMatters: Stuffing 25 retrieved chunks into a 128k-token prompt inflates TTFT from 250 ms to >2,000 ms, multiplies API spend by 5–10x, and degrades answer accuracy due to the 'lost-in-the-middle' U-shaped attention curve.
whenToUse: High-volume RAG pipelines retrieving 15–50 candidate chunks across hybrid BM25 + dense vector search.
Latency-sensitive conversational agents where KV-cache prefill exceeds your 500 ms TTFT SLO.
Multi-hop QA or enterprise search over verbose PDFs, legal contracts, or Slack threads packed with boilerplate.
whenNotToUse: Exact verbatim tasks (legal clause auditing, regex/code diffing) where dropping a single qualifier alters meaning.
Small-context lookups where total retrieved text is already under 1,500 tokens.
When your compressor is a slow autoregressive LLM call that adds 1.5s of latency just to save 400 ms of downstream prefill.
keyPoints: Reranking (cross-encoder) eliminates irrelevant chunks at the document level, whereas context compression eliminates redundant tokens *inside* relevant chunks.
Extractive sentence pruning (e.g., RECOMP-Extractive, Sentence-BERT filtering) preserves verbatim quotes and exact numbers better than abstractive summarization.
Perplexity-based token pruning (LLMLingua-2 using XLM-RoBERTa) achieves 3x–6x compression in ~30–60 ms on a single GPU without calling an autoregressive LLM.
Question-aware compression (LongLLMLingua) conditions token importance on the user query, boosting multi-document QA accuracy by up to 17% over uncompressed long prompts.
Compressed prompts must preserve chunk IDs and metadata headers so inline citation grounding (`[doc_id]`) survives compression.

examples.title: Enterprise Support Copilot on 120-Page Runbooks
examples.scenario: Retrieving top-20 chunks (512 tokens each = ~10,240 tokens) from Qdrant for an SRE incident copilot caused 1.9s TTFT and frequent hallucinations when the key CLI flag sat in chunk #11.
examples.outcome: Adding a 2-stage pipeline—BGE-Reranker-v2-M3 (top 20 -> top 8) followed by LLMLingua-2 (rate=0.45)—cut prompt size to ~1,850 tokens, dropped TTFT to 340 ms, and lifted answer faithfulness from 0.81 to 0.93.

examples.title: Financial 10-K Multi-Hop QA
examples.scenario: Comparing YoY R&D footnotes across 4 SEC filings required retrieving 32,000 tokens of dense prose, exceeding cost budgets at $2.50/1M input tokens.
examples.outcome: Query-conditioned extractive sentence compression retained only sentences with cross-encoder score >0.65 plus surrounding table headers, achieving 5.4x compression and 95.2% numerical exact-match.

tradeOffs.pro: Extractive pruning keeps exact figures, URLs, and identifiers intact with zero hallucination risk.
tradeOffs.con: Can produce choppy, ungrammatical text that slightly hurts fluency if compression exceeds 5x.

tradeOffs.factor: Small Encoder Compressor vs. LLM-Based Extractor
tradeOffs.pro: Encoder models (XLM-RoBERTa / DeBERTa) run in 20–60 ms and cost fractions of a cent per 1k queries.
tradeOffs.con: LLM extractors (`LLMChainExtractor`) understand nuanced multi-sentence logic better, at the cost of 600–1,500 ms extra latency.

tradeOffs.pro: Maximizes throughput and minimizes KV-cache memory pressure on self-hosted vLLM clusters.
tradeOffs.con: Aggressive pruning risks stripping negations ('not', 'except') or conditional units ('per month' vs 'per year').

failureModes.name: Negation & Qualifier Stripping
failureModes.description: Token-level compressors drop low-perplexity function words like 'not', 'unless', or 'deprecated', flipping policy rules.
failureModes.mitigation: Use sentence-level or span-level constraints (LLMLingua-2 force_tokens) and never prune syntactic negation tokens.

failureModes.name: Broken Citation Mapping
failureModes.description: Abstractive summarization merges three chunks into one paragraph, making it impossible to trace which source URL backed a claim.
failureModes.mitigation: Compress each chunk independently inside `<doc id="...">` wrappers and re-attach source metadata post-compression.

failureModes.name: Latency Inversion
failureModes.description: Running a 7B compressor sequentially on CPU or calling an external LLM API takes longer than sending the raw 15k tokens directly to a fast Flash model.
failureModes.mitigation: Benchmark end-to-end TTFT; use lightweight DeBERTa/XLM-RoBERTa encoders on GPU or batch compression.

failureModes.name: Table & Code Block Corruption
failureModes.description: Pruning whitespace or pipe delimiters inside Markdown tables or JSON snippets breaks structural parsing for the generator LLM.
failureModes.mitigation: Bypass token-level pruning for `<table>` or fenced code blocks, compressing only surrounding narrative prose.

commonMistakes: Skipping a cross-encoder reranker and feeding 30 noisy vector results straight into a token compressor.
Compressing chunks offline at index time without knowing the user query, discarding details needed for future specific questions.
Measuring only compression ratio (e.g., 10x) without tracking downstream RAGAS Faithfulness and Context Recall.
Using abstractive LLM compression on numeric financial or medical records where paraphrasing introduces rounding or unit errors.
Forgetting to reorder surviving chunks (e.g., placing highest-scored chunks at the start and end of the prompt to counter lost-in-the-middle).

sections.content:
## The idea

Even with 128k–1M token context windows, raw RAG retrieval is both economically wasteful and cognitively noisy. Dense embedding models (using cosine similarity over 768–1536d vectors) optimize for broad semantic recall, frequently pulling 512-token chunks where only 40 tokens actually answer the user's question. Feeding all 20 chunks to the generator LLM triggers quadratic/linear KV-cache prefill overhead, inflates Time-to-First-Token (TTFT), and induces the **lost-in-the-middle** phenomenon where models attend strongly to the first and last 10% of the prompt while ignoring middle evidence.

**Context compression** sits between retrieval and generation as an information bottleneck. It operates across two complementary axes: **coarse-grained filtering** (cross-encoder reranking and document-level pruning) and **fine-grained compression** (extractive sentence selection, perplexity-based token pruning like **LLMLingua-2**, or query-focused abstractive distillation like **RECOMP**).

## Concrete walkthrough

Trace a production query—*"What is the retry backoff cap for webhook deliveries in v3?"*—through a 3-stage compressed RAG pipeline:

1. **Hybrid Retrieval**: Qdrant returns top-25 chunks via RRF (BM25 + `bge-large-en-v1.5`), totaling **12,800 tokens**.
2. **Cross-Encoder Rerank**: `BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3` scores all 25 `(query, chunk)` pairs in a single 45 ms GPU batch, discarding 19 low-relevance chunks and keeping the top-6 (**3,100 tokens**).
3. **Query-Aware Fine Compression**: **LLMLingua-2** (XLM-RoBERTa-large token classifier) evaluates token keep-probabilities conditioned on the query, preserving `<doc>` tags, numbers, and negations (`force_tokens=['\n', '.', 'not', 'ms', 's']`) at a 0.45 target ratio. The surviving context shrinks to **1,390 tokens** in 38 ms.
4. **Reorder & Generate**: Surviving chunks are placed in U-shaped order (highest-scored at positions 1 and 6) and sent to the generator LLM, dropping TTFT from 1,420 ms to **290 ms**.

sections.content:
## Extractive, perplexity, and abstractive paradigms

Context compressors fall into three architectural families. **Extractive compressors** (such as `EmbeddingsFilter` or **RECOMP-Extractive**) score individual sentences against the query and drop sentences below a cosine or cross-encoder threshold; they are fast and never invent facts, though they cannot prune verbosity within a long sentence. **Token-level compressors** (**LLMLingua**, **LongLLMLingua**, **LLMLingua-2**) use either causal LLM perplexity or a distilled bidirectional token classifier to remove predictable filler tokens, achieving 4x–10x compression in <50 ms. **Abstractive compressors** (**RECOMP-Abstractive**, LangChain `LLMChainExtractor`) rewrite retrieved passages into dense query-specific notes, offering the highest semantic density at the expense of higher latency and potential paraphrasing drift.

## Compression techniques compared

| Technique | Granularity | Typical Latency | Compression Ratio | Preserves Exact Quotes? | Best For |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **BGE-Reranker-v2-M3** | Chunk-level | 30–60 ms (GPU) | 3x–5x (Top-25 to 5) | Yes | First-stage noise removal in all RAG pipelines |
| **LLMLingua-2 (XLM-R)** | Token-level | 25–55 ms (GPU) | 3x–6x | Partial (drops filler) | High-throughput chat & long-context cost reduction |
| **LongLLMLingua** | Coarse-to-fine | 150–400 ms | 4x–10x | Partial | Multi-document QA with severe lost-in-the-middle |
| **RECOMP-Extractive** | Sentence-level | 20–40 ms | 4x–8x | Yes | Compliance, legal, and citation-strict enterprise QA |
| **LLMChainExtractor** | Abstractive | 700–1,800 ms | 5x–15x | No (paraphrased) | Offline batch synthesis or messy multi-turn transcripts |

## Failure modes

The subtlest failure mode is **semantic inversion via token deletion**: if a token-level pruner drops `'not'`, `'except'`, or `'beta'` from a policy sentence, the generator confidently asserts the opposite rule. Another common breakdown is **structural corruption**, where pruning pipe characters (`|`) or indentation destroys Markdown tables and JSON payloads. Finally, **over-compression** past 8x often strips entity coreferences (e.g., removing the subject header while keeping `'It supports 10k RPS'`), causing the generator to attribute a metric to the wrong microservice.

## Evaluation and KV-cache economics

Never optimize compression ratio in isolation. Evaluate on a 200+ query golden set using **RAGAS** metrics—specifically *Context Precision*, *Context Recall*, and *Faithfulness*—alongside p95 end-to-end TTFT. In self-hosted **vLLM** or **TensorRT-LLM** deployments, context compression directly increases max concurrent batch size by freeing GPU HBM from bloated KV-caches. As a rule of thumb, target the knee of the curve: **3x–5x total reduction** (rerank + fine prune) typically retains >97% of uncompressed EM/F1 while cutting TTFT and input token spend by 65–80%.

## Practical checklist

- Always run a **cross-encoder reranker** (e.g., BGE-Reranker-v2-M3 or Cohere Rerank) before token/sentence compression.
- Wrap each chunk in `<doc id="..." url="...">` tags and lock structural delimiters via `force_tokens`.
- Exclude fenced code blocks and Markdown tables from token-level pruning.
- Benchmark compressor latency on target hardware to verify `T_compress + T_prefill_compressed < T_prefill_raw`.
- Apply **LongContextReorder** (highest-ranked chunks at the beginning and end of the prompt) before calling the generator.
- Track RAGAS Faithfulness and exact-number accuracy on every compression ratio change.

interviewProblems.title: Context Compression for RAG
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Design a production system that depends on Context Compression for RAG. What invariants, failure modes, and observability do you require?
interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Start from invariants, choose the pattern that preserves them, and add metrics for the known failure modes.
commonPitfalls: Optimizing throughput before defining correctness boundaries.

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: Techniques that prune, rerank, or summarize retrieved RAG chunks before LLM generation to slash token cost and TTFT while beating 'lost-in-the-middle' attention decay.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: Token / Span Compressor applies the primary invariant and coordinates with Generator LLM.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, Generator LLM experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Use sentence-level or span-level constraints (LLMLingua-2 force_tokens) and never prune syntactic negation tokens.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Pair a fast cross-encoder reranker (BGE-Reranker-v2-M3) with token-level or extractive compression (LLMLingua-2 / RECOMP) to shrink 20k+ retrieved tokens down to 2k–3k high-signal tokens without losing exact citations.
Avoid trap: Skipping a cross-encoder reranker and feeding 30 noisy vector results straight into a token compressor.
Avoid trap: Compressing chunks offline at index time without knowing the user query, discarding details needed for future specific questions.
When to reach for it: High-volume RAG pipelines retrieving 15–50 candidate chunks across hybrid BM25 + dense vector search.
When to reach for it: Latency-sensitive conversational agents where KV-cache prefill exceeds your 500 ms TTFT SLO.

putItTogether.title: Putting Context Compression Rag Together
putItTogether.summary: Pair a fast cross-encoder reranker (BGE-Reranker-v2-M3) with token-level or extractive compression (LLMLingua-2 / RECOMP) to shrink 20k+ retrieved tokens down to 2k–3k high-signal tokens without losing exact citations.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Context Compression Rag before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: Adding a 2-stage pipeline—BGE-Reranker-v2-M3 (top 20 -> top 8) followed by LLMLingua-2 (rate=0.45)—cut prompt size to ~1,850 tokens, dropped TTFT to 340 ms, and lifted answer faithfulness from 0.81 to 0.93.
